main_text.p: origo traditionis. Jam antè Origenem, creditus Lucas Epistolæ interpres & translator. Clemens Alexandrinus diserte, τὸν Λουκᾶν αὐτὴν μεθερμηνευόμενον [?], ἐκδοῦναι τοῖς Ἕλλησι [?]. Ex translationis ergo fama, orta de scriptione ipsa suspicio. Nec nisi de scriptione secundaria, & per translationis modum, Origenis verba accipienda esse putem. Quomodo de Evangelio Marci Tertullianus, contrà Marcion. L. iv. Et Marcus quod edidit, Petri affirmatur, cujus interpres Marcus.

IV. Tertiò, ne Lucæ quidem fuit, similli Epistola convenire Hebræorū Ecclesias. Apostolicæ id fuit authoritatis&prærogativæ. Et à solis Apostolis profectæ, quas canonicas habemus hodieque. Nec eadem, ut monebamus, conscribendæ Historiæ, quæ Epistolæ ratio fuit. Ad illam φιλοσοφίᾳ τῶν πραγμάτων [?], & internus spiritus S. ductus & afflatus, ad hanc etiā authoritas externa, & Apostolica, & Ecclesiæ universalis cura, requisita. page.notes: Greek words in the second and fourth lines are small and partly blurred; the Greek letters are my best reading and are marked [?]. The word "similli" in the text appears to be printed as "similli" (misprint for "similis" or the printed form as seen). The printed "Hebræorû" has a tilde over the final u, copied as ū. The printed "etiā" has a macron over the a, kept as printed. "Lucæ" and "Lucas" are set in italics. The page has no marginal notes.
